Contributing 14% to the U.S. crude oil supply, the Gulf is home to some of the world’s lowest carbon intensity oil and natural gas. With a more than 85-year track record of success in the Gulf, Chevron is continuing to grow operations there. Our goal is to produce 300,000 net barrels of oil-equivalent per day in 2026. play pause video play pause video Leading the way in deepwater A history of growth Over the years, Chevron has continued to innovate in the Gulf of America. Thanks to technological advances, we can now safely access and develop deeper and higher-pressure resources than ever before. Industry leader In 1938, Chevron legacy companies brought the first shallow offshore well online in the Gulf. This set the stage for future exploration. Reaching the unreachable In the 1970s and 1980s, Chevron transitioned to deepwater drilling. Using emerging technologies, we safely explored depths previously considered unreachable. Going deeper In the 2000s, Chevron began ultra-deepwater projects. This showcased a commitment to fresh approaches and operational excellence. Technological edge Chevron’s Anchor Project, which started production in 2024, uses industry-leading high-pressure subsea technology. This helps safely produce energy from deeper reservoirs and higher pressures. Increased presence: In 2025, Chevron’s acquisition of Hess built on Chevron’s position as the largest leaseholder in the Gulf. With this expanded presence and combined assets, we aim to strengthen efficiency. Gulf of America in action A closer look at Chevron’s portfolio Chevron’s oil and natural gas production in the Gulf of America helps meet the world’s energy needs. Today, with large fields, stacked reservoirs, and new drilling and production capabilities, Chevron is a leading performer in the GOA. Our assets include nine operated facilities and multiple tiebacks. We’re the leading leaseholder in the Gulf, and a significant portion of our undeveloped acreage is within tieback range. Technology We’re using technology to increase production, help predict geologic factors more effectively and access hard-to-reach reserves. Standardization With standardized processes, tools and equipment, along with repeatable engineering solutions, we’re helping to boost efficiency, lower costs and reduce cycle times. “We’re leveraging our strengths in the Gulf of America to help meet energy demand and bolster U.S. energy security.” Brent Gros | President, Offshore business A vision for continued growth Building on our record of success in the region, Chevron is well positioned to continue growing affordable, reliable Gulf of America production. Looking forward, the GOA is expected to play an important role in future U.S. energy supply.
